newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks firm in London, Boeing rises.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks firm in London, Boeing rises.

text.p: U.S. stocks were generally firmer in London, though trading was thin ahead of the triple expiration of index futures and options in the U.S. later on Friday, dealers said.

Trading was thin as European investors stood on the sidelines amid a dearth of fresh factors and ahead of so-called "triple-witching" expiration, which is expected to add volatility into an already choppy market.
"The market still looks good, but no one seems to want to do anything at the moment," said one London dealer. "There are very few features."
Among them, shares in Boeing Co added $1/4 in London to $56-3/4 after British Airways Plc confirmed it placed a $1 billion order with Boeing.

Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc climbed $1/8 to $47-1/2 after jumping $1-7/8 in New York on Thursday, among hopes for an agreement in U.S. talks aimed at a settlement of lawsuits over smoking-related diseases.
The September S&P 500 futures were up 2.05 points to 909.55 on Globex at 1027 GMT. The U.S. September T-bond future slipped 2/32 to 112-4/32.
Dealers here were expecting Wall Street to open higher, but said it was vulnerable to profit-taking ahead of expiry.
